content: 1. Is the facility equipped with an information system to manage occupational safety and health during storm events? 2. Does the facility have an emergency plan in place to protect healthcare workers from multiple biological and chemical hazards during a storm? 3. Is there a post-storm employee recovery assistance program tailored to the needs of the staff? 4. Are personnel, especially clean-up crews, provided with full personal protective equipment (PPE), including waterproof safety boots, goggles, work gloves, and masks? 5. Is safe water and food available to staff and patients during storm events? 6. Are healthcare workers trained on public health and climate change hazards, including health impacts associated with various types of storms? 7. Are healthcare workers actively involved in the development of plans and responses to storm risks? 8. Are staff prepared and capable of implementing risk reduction actions to protect themselves during storm events? 9. Are healthcare workers trained to manage hazardous chemicals in emergency situations? 10. Are staff trained in conducting multi-hazard assessments? 11. Is there a safe internal communication system in place, particularly for emergency situations? 12. Are healthcare workers aware of contingency plans for accessing and leaving the facility during flood or strong wind emergencies, including transportation for the health workforce? 13. Is the facility prepared with clear messaging on water and food safety during and after a storm? 14. Does the facility have a community health education program to assist the community in reducing vulnerability to storm impacts? 15. Is there a community health education program aimed at improving community health in the face of storm risks? 16. Does the facility assess the capacity of its stormwater management system to handle anticipated 50or 100-year storm events? 17. Are sanitation systems regularly assessed for potential damage during storms and severe winds? 18. Does the facility have information on water system installations that minimize the risk of contamination? 19. Are sewer overflows monitored, and are pumps repaired in advance of and after storm events? 20. Does the facility have a stormwater management system capable of mitigating storm-induced flooding? 21. Is there a stormwater management system in place to prevent standing water near the facility? 22. Is there a schedule for emptying latrines in advance of storms to prevent overflows? 23. Are water storage tanks supported and anchored to withstand strong winds and heavy rainfall? 24. Is there a safe system for waste disposal after a storm? 25. Does the facility have a safe management approach for transporting healthcare waste, including hazardous waste, during and after a storm? 26. Is there on-site water purification equipment to provide safe drinking water? 27. Does the facility have an assessment plan to map risks to water and sanitation infrastructures, identifying potential service disruptions during storms, floods, and landslides? 28. Are priority areas within the facility identified for emergency power needs? 29. Is renewable energy, such as solar power, assessed for its sufficiency in powering critical equipment? 30. Are appliance thermometers available in refrigerators and freezers to ensure the safety of food, vaccines, and other refrigeration-dependent medical supplies? 31. Is there adequate daylight to ensure proper visibility during power outages? 32. Are power-operated doors capable of being manually opened during power failures? 33. Is there an emergency plan for power outages, addressing shortand long-term scenarios before, during, and after a storm? 34. Does the facility collaborate with energy utility agencies to prevent electricity service suspensions? 35. Is there a management plan for intermittent energy supplies or system failures? 36. Are there plans or regulations in place to reduce overall energy consumption? 37. Does the facility work with local governments to support vulnerable populations in participating in risk reduction management, policymaking, planning, and implementation? 38. Are climate risk and vulnerability assessments conducted for all facility sectors to identify risk scenarios, vulnerabilities, and response capacities? 39. Is there a monitoring and early warning system to manage and reduce storm-related health risks? 40. Is assessed information used as a basis for planning and prioritizing measures to reduce risk impacts? 41. Does the facility consider how climate risks may evolve in the future during annual planning? 42. Are resources available to adopt risk reduction measures for the building, infrastructure, technologies, products, and processes? 43. Are assessments regularly updated to incorporate emerging scientific information? 44. Is there a plan for relocating medical devices, medicines, mobile equipment, and other supplies in case of operational disruptions or outbreaks? 45. Is there a mechanism for prompt maintenance and repair of equipment required for essential services? 46. Are procedures in place to store food and bottled water safely above potential flood levels? 47. Are there established procedures for procuring, transporting, and storing bottled water and food supplies during emergencies? 48. Are there established procedures for procuring, transporting, and safely storing medical devices, vaccines, pharmaceuticals, parenteral nutrition, and blood supplies? 49. Are the performance and vulnerabilities of critical facility components (structural and non-structural) assessed for storm hazards? 50. Are potential losses calculated, and measures implemented to reduce impacts? 51. Is there a plan to house staff at the facility if shelter-in-place is required, including sleeping rooms, food, and water? 52. Are machine rooms resistant to flooding or high wind/rooftop damage? 53. Are stairwells fortified against high-wind events? 54. Are measures in place to remove mosquito breeding sites? 55. Are windows and doors leak-proof and equipped with wind protection devices? 56. Are walls protected and insulated against moisture and mold? 57. Are equipment and power supplies removed from basements and ground floors to avoid flood damage? 58. Are agreements in place with other healthcare providers for additional health services and clinical resources? 59. Is there a plan for continuity of operational processes during a storm and for building back better through training and workshops? 60. Are site and building maintenance procedures conducted with specifications on how weather may affect the facility's safety and functionality? 61. Is there a space within or external to the facility for storing and stockpiling additional supplies, considering access, security, temperature, ventilation, light exposure, and humidity? 62. Is there an information system between the health sector and meteorological services to communicate about climate hazards? 63. Are electronic patient health records available to other receiving facilities in case of evacuation? 64. Is information and communication flow ensured between the health workforce and policymakers, particularly during high-stress situations and emergencies? 65. Is there an information system for tracking and monitoring diseases following storm events? 66. Is adaptive governance capacity improved for evaluating and implementing measures for risk identification, reduction, and response? 67. Are trees planted in secure locations to avoid blocking access to the facility or falling on the building during storm events? 68. Are partnerships established between the facility, community, and local authorities to identify and reduce vulnerabilities in surrounding areas? 69. Is there an access route for public transportation likely to remain operational during or immediately following a storm event? 70. Are estimates available for the consumption of essential medical, pharmaceutical, nutritional, and laboratory supplies, as well as personal protective equipment, food, etc.? 71. Are risk assessments conducted for the supply chain of essential medical and non-medical products? 72. Is there a secure plan to ensure continuity of the facility’s supply and delivery chain? 73. Is secure access to essential backup services, such as sterilization, laundry, and cleaning services, ensured through multiple agreements with different facilities to maintain critical services during or immediately following a storm event? This version is structured to provide clarity and precision, ensuring it is accessible to healthcare professionals and stakeholders involved in emergency preparedness and response.
